newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2985 against the U.S. dollar on Friday from Thursday's 8.2999 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market with lower intervention by the central bank, traders said.
Dealers said that the People's Bank of China was seen reducing its intervention in the yuan at about 8.30, which made the yuan remain on its uptrend.

The yuan opened little changed at 8.2998 and hit an intra-day low of 8.3000 early in the session. It then rose to move between 8.2980 and 8.2985 for the rest of the session, reaching a high of 8.2975.
Trading was active, with most done at about 8.2980, traders said.
"Little selling emerged around the key 8.3000 resistance level which was breached yesterday," one dealer said.
"The central bank usually sells the yuan to prevent its rise, which it thinks is an effective way of controlling inflation," said a second dealer.
"Less active selling indicates that intervention by the central bank was weaker," he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to try to stand above 8.30 early next week.
The yuan closed up slightly at 7.2843 from 7.2995 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intra-day high of 1.0723 from 1.0740 against the Hong Kong dollar.
